title: Tensor square for the localized system clopen arrow before proper mates
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $K$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(K.k)$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. For every scheme $W$, use the strict quotient-semilinear system category and its ordinary unbounded derived category $D_W$ of [def-pur-system-tensor-mate-arrows], with quotient exponent $n+1$, and any normalized tensor operations $o$ of that node. Let $A,B,C,F$ be separated finite-type $K.k$-schemes, $k:A\to B$ and $i:C\to F$ quasi-compact open immersions, $r:A\to C$ and $p:B\to F$ proper, all morphisms over $K.k$, with $p\circ k=i\circ r$. Write $P,J,T,\mu,\delta,\alpha$ for the specified pullback, exact open extension, tensor, tensor pullback comparison, open tensor comparison and localized clopen arrow of that node. Let $c:P_kP_p\cong P_rP_i$ be its canonical square comparison. For every $G\in D_C$, $Q\in D_F$, the following equality holds in $D_B$, before evaluation: $P_p(\delta_{i;G,Q});\alpha_{T_C(G,P_iQ)};J_k(\mu_{r;G,P_iQ}) = \mu_{p;J_iG,Q};T_B(\alpha_G,1);\delta_{k;P_rG,P_pQ};J_k(T_A(1,c_Q))$. Both sides have source $P_pT_F(J_iG,Q)$ and target $J_kT_A(P_rG,P_rP_iQ)$. Semicolons denote composition in displayed order. The square need not be cartesian; no boundedness, Tor, coefficient flatness or cartesianness condition on the systems is assumed. This statement involves no proper-adjunction mate or projection morphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-system-tensor-presentation-identification] to identify the canonical ringed-sequence tensor, pullback, open extension and their unit/counit-normalized comparisons with the supplied operations o. Its representative normalization fixes mu, delta and the pullback compositors on whole systems, rather than only after evaluation.

Apply [lem-pur-system-clopen-mate-identification] to identify o.alpha with open base change beta, b_! of the identity/zero projector for s=(k,r):A→B×[F]C, and the canonical open/pullback compositors. Only its alpha identification is needed, not its proper-mate clause.

Use the full tensor-comparison identity of [lem-sf-clopen-comparison-tensor-square] in systems mode for this clopen word. Its Cartesian beta square follows by fully faithful open restriction and open-unit normalization. Its clopen square is the (identity,zero) projector tensor identity; its composite-open identity identifies delta_b followed by b_!delta_s with delta_k. Substituting the comparisons of the first two steps gives the displayed identity, with c:P_kP_p→P_rP_i on the right. All localizations and representative comparisons are on whole unbounded systems.

theorem system_clopen_alpha_tensor_square
    (K : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ K.p)
    (E : Type (u + 1)) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (o : TensorOperations l E)
    {A B C F : Scheme.{u}}
    [A.Over (Spec (.of K.k))] [B.Over (Spec (.of K.k))]
    [C.Over (Spec (.of K.k))] [F.Over (Spec (.of K.k))]
    [IsSeparated (A ↘ Spec (.of K.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (A ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (A ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [IsSeparated (B ↘ Spec (.of K.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (B ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (B ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [IsSeparated (C ↘ Spec (.of K.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (C ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (C ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [IsSeparated (F ↘ Spec (.of K.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (F ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (F ↘ Spec (.of K.k))]
    (k : A ⟶ B) (r : A ⟶ C) (p : B ⟶ F) (i : C ⟶ F)
    [k.IsOver (Spec (.of K.k))] [r.IsOver (Spec (.of K.k))]
    [p.IsOver (Spec (.of K.k))] [i.IsOver (Spec (.of K.k))]
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i]
    [IsProper r] [IsProper p] (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i)
    (G : D l E C) (Q : D l E F) :
    (o.P p).map ((o.delta i G Q).hom) ≫
        (o.alpha k r p i h).app ((o.T C).obj (G, (o.P i).obj Q)) ≫
        (o.J k).map ((o.mu r).hom.app (G, (o.P i).obj Q)) =
      (o.mu p).hom.app ((o.J i).obj G, Q) ≫
        (o.T B).map (Prod.mkHom ((o.alpha k r p i h).app G) (𝟙 ((o.P p).obj Q))) ≫
        (o.delta k ((o.P r).obj G) ((o.P p).obj Q)).hom ≫
        (o.J k).map ((o.T A).map
          (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 ((o.P r).obj G)) ((o.square k r p i h).hom.app Q)))
